Contributor Guide: Adding Permanent Model Families

Source: vignettes/articles/contributor-guide-adding-permanent-model-families.Rmd
contributor-guide-adding-permanent-model-families.Rmd

This guide outlines the systematic procedure for contributing a new model family as a permanent, first-class citizen in the MVBeliefUpdatr core.

1. Motivation: Family Registration vs. First-Class Core Classes

While MVBeliefUpdatr supports lightweight custom model families via new_mvbu_family() and general MVBU_CategoryRepresentation instances, promoting frequently used or foundational families to core built-in classes provides significant engineering advantages:

  1. IDE Tab Completion and Discoverability: Dedicated constructor functions (such as new_uvg_category_representation() and new_niw_category_representation()) feature explicit, typed arguments that autocomplete seamlessly in IDEs.
  2. Strict Property Validation at Construction: Concrete S7 classes validate domain constraints immediately upon instantiation (e.g., positive variance, symmetric covariance matrices, probability distributions summing to 1).
  3. High-Performance S7 Method Dispatch: Direct S7 class hierarchy dispatch avoids reflective introspection of metadata or property names at runtime.
  4. Integration with Compiled Stan Generative Models: Built-in classes can interface directly with precompiled Stan models and C++ routines for Bayesian parameter estimation.

2. Architecture and Design Principles

Every built-in model family adheres to the following structural conventions:

  1. Family Descriptors (MVBU_Family): Model families are registered in .build_builtin_families() within R/S7-class.R. Each family encapsulates:

    • density_function: Pure mathematical density function supporting perceptual noise treatments ("no_noise", "sample", "marginalize").
    • sampling_function: Vectorized random number generator.
    • expected_moments: Extraction of first and second moments (mu, Sigma).
    • default_prior: Standard prior configuration constructor.
    • stanmodel: Optional list specifying stanmodel_name (e.g., "NIX_ideal_adaptor") and stanfit_class (e.g., "NIX_IdealAdaptorStanfit"), or NULL if no Stan model is associated.

  2. Internal Likelihood Closure Parity: Concrete category representation constructors do not handwrite custom closure math. Instead, they instantiate the S7 class and uniformly derive the category likelihood closure directly from the family descriptor:

    rep <- MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation(...)
rep@category_likelihood_function <- .make_family_likelihood_function(rep)

  3. Base-Class-First Logic: Package methods and algorithms target the base class MVBU_CategoryRepresentation. Specialized methods are only implemented where mathematical optimizations (such as Cholesky prefactorization) warrant concrete overrides.

3. Step-by-Step Implementation Procedure

Step 1: Author S7 Class and Constructors (R/S7-class-{family}.R)

Create a dedicated file R/S7-class-{family}.R containing: 1. S7 class definition inheriting from MVBU_CategoryRepresentation. 2. S7 validator enforcing strict domain constraints. 3. Constructor new_{family}_category_representation() using .make_family_likelihood_function(rep). 4. Empirical constructor new_{family}_category_representation_from_data().

#' @rdname family-myfamily
#' @export
new_myfamily_category_representation <- function(
  category_labels,
  cue_labels,
  param1,
  param2,
  metadata = list()
) {
  # Rationale for retaining typed class constructor:
  # Concrete typed constructors provide strict property validation, IDE tab
  # completion, and fast S7 method dispatch, while obtaining the likelihood
  # closure uniformly from the registered model family density function.
  rep <- MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation(
    category_likelihood_function = NULL,
    metadata = set_labels(
      metadata,
      cue = as.character(cue_labels),
      category = as.character(category_labels),
      response_category = as.character(category_labels),
      group = if (!is.null(metadata$group)) {
        as.character(metadata$group)
      } else {
        character(0)
      }
    ),
    param1 = as.numeric(param1),
    param2 = as.numeric(param2)
  )
  rep@category_likelihood_function <- .make_family_likelihood_function(rep)
  rep
}

Step 2: Register Family Descriptor (R/S7-class.R)

In R/S7-class.R, add the family registration inside .build_builtin_families():

"MYFAMILY" = new_mvbu_family(
  family_names = list(
    name_short = "MYFAMILY",
    name_full = "My Family Distribution",
    name_category_representation = "MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation",
    name_category_representation_template =
      "MyFamily_CategoryRepresentationTemplate",
    name_cognitive_model = "MyFamily_Model"
  ),
  description = "Description of family.",
  density_function = function(
    x, rep, log = FALSE,
    noise_treatment = "no_noise",
    Sigma_noise = NULL
  ) {
    # Vectorized density evaluation supporting noise treatment
  },
  sampling_function = function(rep, n = 1L) {
    # Vectorized random draw generation
  },
  expected_moments = function(rep) {
    list(mu = ..., Sigma = ...)
  },
  stanmodel = list(
    stanmodel_name = "MYFAMILY_ideal_adaptor",
    stanfit_class = "MYFAMILY_IdealAdaptorStanfit"
  ) # or NULL if analytic
)

Ensure .get_family_from_class_name() maps MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation to "MYFAMILY".

Step 3: Implement S7 Methods (R/S7-methods.R)

Register specific S7 methods if specialized behavior is required:

  • get_parameters(MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation)
  • sample_observations(MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation)
  • If dynamic adaptor: update_template(MyFamily_Model)

Step 4: Develop Unit Tests (tests/testthat/)

  1. Create tests/testthat/test-XX-S7-{family}.R covering:

    • Object creation and validator edge cases.
    • Likelihood evaluation against reference distributions.
    • Noise treatment modes ("no_noise", "sample", "marginalize").
    • Expected moments and sampling fidelity.

  2. Verify cross-family parity by running:

    testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-17-S7-model-cross-family-parity.R")

4. Documentation & Packaging Standards

The package documentation is strictly governed by roxygen2 conventions:

4.1 Roxygen Rd Grouping & Naming Conventions

  1. Grouping via @rdname: Group semantically related functions, classes, and methods onto a single unified manual topic. For instance, all constructors and accessors for MyFamily should share:

    #' @rdname family-myfamily
#' @family model families

  2. Cross-Linking with @seealso: Explicitly link related model families, constructors, and mathematical methods. Example:

    #' @seealso \code{\link{new_mvg_category_representation}},
#'   \code{\link{get_family}}, \code{\link{evaluate_model}}

  3. Internal Helpers: Internal functions must start with a leading dot (.my_internal_helper), specify @keywords internal, and omit export tags (or use @noRd if no manual page is generated).

4.2 S7 Class Documentation

All S7 class definitions must include comprehensive documentation: - Mark class topics with #' @docType class and #' @export. - Document every property/slot using #' @property <name> <description>. - In constructor functions, document all parameters with their types, constraints, and explicit defaults (e.g., (default: 0)).

4.3 File Ordering and @include Dependencies

Because roxygen2 manages Collate ordering for S7 class hierarchies, declare inter-file dependencies explicitly at the top of each R file:

#' @include S7-class.R
#' @include S7-generics.R
#' @include S7-class-myfamily.R
NULL

Always verify that parent classes and generics precede their child classes and method definitions in the @include statements.

5. Coercion Architecture (.mvbu_coerce_category_representation)

MVBeliefUpdatr provides seamless cross-family conversion via .mvbu_coerce_category_representation() and its template counterpart .mvbu_coerce_category_representation_template() in R/S7-family-coercion.R.

5.1 Conversion Pathways

  1. Identity (Same Family): If from == to, the object returns unaltered.
  2. Matched Point/Uncertain Pairs:
    • UVG <-> NIX
    • MUVG <-> MNIX
    • MVG <-> NIW Coercing from point (e.g., MVG) to belief distribution (e.g., NIW) requires explicit confidence parameters kappa and nu:
    • Mean center: m = mu
    • Scale matrix: S = Sigma * (nu - D - 1) Coercing from belief to point converts expected moments:
    • mu = m
    • Sigma = S / (nu - D - 1)
  3. Arbitrary Family <-> EXEMPLAR:
    • Parametric to Exemplar: Generates n random points via the family’s vectorized sampling_function().
    • Exemplar to Parametric: Computes sample moments (x_mean, x_css) from stored exemplar points.

5.2 Integrating New Families into Coercion

When introducing a permanent family: 1. Define whether it has a matched point/uncertain counterpart. 2. Register the family token in the allowed vector in R/S7-family-coercion.R. 3. Provide dedicated coercion wrappers: r as_myfamily_category_representation <- function(x, ...) { .mvbu_coerce_category_representation(x, to = "MYFAMILY", ...) } 4. Verify coercion parity in tests/testthat/test-07-S7-as-family.R.

6. Stanfit Ecosystem Integration

Permanent cognitive models intended for Bayesian estimation integrate with the compiled Stan infrastructure:

6.1 Stan Generative Programs (inst/stan/)

  • Place Stan programs in inst/stan/{family}_ideal_adaptor.stan.
  • Ensure the family’s stanmodel$stanmodel_name property matches the Stan program basename without .stan extension (e.g., "NIX_ideal_adaptor"), and stanmodel$stanfit_class matches the Stanfit S7 class name (e.g., "NIX_IdealAdaptorStanfit").
  • Registering the family dynamically populates bidirectional lookups (.to_stanmodel() and .to_family()) in .mvbu_family_registry.
  • Use shared licensing/data chunks via #include statements in inst/stan/include/.
  • Ensure headers compile automatically into C++ exports in src/stanExports_{family}_ideal_adaptor.h via rstantools.

6.2 Data Builders and Input Structures

  1. Raw Frame Preparation: Implement preprocessing within .prepare_staninput_frame() in R/S7-stanfit-input.R, ensuring cues, categories, and group factors are strictly validated and aligned.
  2. Typed Staninput Class: Define MyFamily_IdealAdaptorStaninput in R/S7-staninput.R inheriting from IdealAdaptorStaninput.
  3. Data Summarization: Implement .summarize_exposure() and .summarize_test() blocks mapping observations into numeric arrays, matrices, and sufficient statistics.

6.3 Parameter Extraction and Translation Tables

Stan parameter draws must translate seamlessly into cognitive model moments:

  1. Map Stan parameter vectors (e.g., m, S, kappa, nu) into standardized moments in .compute_exposure_category_statistic() in R/S7-stanfit-methods.R.
  2. Implement model reconstruction hooks in .reconstruct_model_list() in R/S7-stanfit-postprocess.R to reconstruct MVBU_CognitiveModel instances from posterior draws.

7. Testing & Quality Assurance Standards

7.1 Standard Test Fixtures

To guarantee fast, deterministic tests without duplicating data fixtures:

  • pb52: Standard Peterson & Barney (1952) vowel formant dataset (1D and 2D formant cues F1, F2).
  • mixer6: 6-talker acoustic exposure dataset for multi-group and talker adaptation scenarios.
  • Package Generators: Use standard generators rather than ad-hoc setups:
    • example_exposure_test_data()
    • example_ideal_adaptor_stanfit_input()
    • example_ideal_adaptor_staninput()
    • example_mvg_ideal_observer()
    • example_niw_ideal_adaptor()
  • Pre-fitted MCMC Models: Store serialized test fits strictly in tests/testthat/models/. Never run long MCMC chains during unit test runs.

7.2 Parameter Recovery Testing

Every new estimator or Stan model must demonstrate parameter recovery:

  1. Simulate known true parameters using the family’s sampling_function().
  2. Fit the model or calculate analytic updates.
  3. Assert that estimated parameters fall within nominal error tolerances (e.g., 95% posterior credible intervals or analytical equivalence).

7.3 Parity Snapshots and Cross-Family Parity

Verify that the new family produces expected likelihoods and classifications consistent with analytical baselines by adding test expectations to: - tests/testthat/test-17-S7-model-cross-family-parity.R - tests/testthat/test-01-S7-classes.R

8. Quality Assurance & Phase-End Verification Checklist

Before opening a pull request, ensure every item on this checklist is satisfied:

  • devtools::test()

  • rmarkdown::render(
  "vignettes/extending-mvbeliefupdatr-adding-model-families.Rmd"
)

  • testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-17-S7-model-cross-family-parity.R")
